sub_questions.question: Why does the workspace say it is out of credits when the app hasn't been used much?
Can you fix the out-of-credits problem?

claims.claim: The credit allowance is different depending on the plan.
claims.guide_evidence: Sandbox | Free | 200 credits, one-time (does not renew) ... Professional ... 5,000 credits/month ... Team ... 10,000 credits/month

claims.claim: The free Sandbox plan includes 200 message credits.
claims.guide_evidence: Sandbox | Free | 200 credits, one-time (does not renew)

claims.claim: Sandbox credits top back up at the start of every month.
A Sandbox user who waits a few days will have their balance restored.
Professional and Team plan credits reset monthly.
claims.guide_evidence: waits for the next monthly credit reset (paid plans)

claims.claim: Running out mid-cycle usually means a heavier model consumed the balance faster than expected, because some responses cost more credits than others.
claims.guide_evidence: A workspace that mostly uses a heavier model will exhaust its credit balance noticeably faster than the headline credit number suggests.

claims.claim: The Billing page shows the workspace's plan and remaining credits.
claims.guide_evidence: Only the workspace owner and admins can open the Billing page and manage a subscription.

claims.claim: Connecting your own provider key is an option for restoring model access.
claims.guide_evidence: model calls on Dify-hosted credits stop working until the workspace either connects its own API key for that provider

claims.claim: Upgrading is an option for getting more credits.

customer_safety_issues: Tells a Sandbox user their credits will refill monthly and that they can simply wait, which the guide explicitly contradicts.
evaluation.rationale: The answer says Sandbox credits refill every month and tells the customer to wait a few days. The guide says Sandbox credits are one-time and do not reset, so a Sandbox user would wait for a refill that never comes. The explanation about heavier models and the paid-plan details are correct, and asking which plan the customer is on is reasonable, but the wrong Sandbox entitlement makes this critical.
